# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:**
Reese Mercado
Member ID: W529317483
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-01 — Reference number POC-8AD74FF769-66861**
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (Partial Knee Replacement section) — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing Cigna's denial of the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) requested for me by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist. The notice dated 2026-08-01 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure, because the records already in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the clinical record submitted with the prior authorization supports that recommendation.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

The plan's guideline states:

> "unicompartmental replacement is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

It then lists, among those criteria:

> "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) ◦ loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration ◦ Criteria exception:"

Here is how my records match that language, point by point.

**Loss of knee function that interferes with activities of daily living.** My records document 24 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake three to four times a night because of the pain. My examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. These are daily, ordinary activities — stairs and sleep — that my knee no longer allows me to manage normally.

**Function-limiting pain at short distances.** My chart documents the functional losses described above. If Cigna requires a specific recorded walking distance in addition to those findings, my surgeon's office can supply it: [walking distance documented at office visit — to be provided by Dr. Lindqvist's office, if requested].

**Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three months.** This criterion is met well beyond the three-month threshold:

- **NSAIDs for 8 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy**, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07 — 8 weeks, 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18**, which gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief.

Taken together, that is a documented course of provider-directed non-surgical care lasting far longer than three months, and it did not resolve my symptoms. Because that care was tried and failed, I am not relying on the policy's exception language — "Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate." and "The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate." — which applies to patients who did not undergo such care. I did.

## About the imaging finding

The stated reason for denial concerns imaging. My MRI of 2026-06-08 reports full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. That is end-stage arthritic change confined to a single compartment — the medial compartment — which is the clinical picture a medial unicompartmental (partial) knee replacement is designed to treat.

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about one thing: the excerpts of the Partial Knee Replacement section that I have been able to obtain do not include a specific imaging requirement or imaging threshold, so I am not quoting plan language on that point and I am not characterizing what the guideline says about imaging. The paragraph above is my own description of my MRI report as written. If Cigna's determination rests on an imaging criterion within this guideline, I respectfully ask that the reconsideration decision identify that criterion by name and explain how my 2026-06-08 MRI findings were measured against it, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it directly.

## Other factors

My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Cigna to overturn the denial issued on 2026-08-01 (reference POC-8AD74FF769-66861) and approve coverage for the partial knee replacement, CPT 27446, as requested by Dr. Lindqvist. If the denial is maintained, I ask that Cigna provide a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion in the Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 guideline that my records were found not to meet, along with the credentials of the reviewer who made that determination, and information about my right to further review.

I understand that my appeal must be received by **2027-01-28**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal through **my.cigna.com**, using my plan's appeal form, and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. If anything further is needed from me, I can be reached at the phone number above, or Cigna may contact me at **1-800-244-6224** or the number on my member ID card to tell me what is missing.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**[Signature]**

Reese Mercado
Member ID: W529317483
[Date of birth]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-01 (Ref. POC-8AD74FF769-66861)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-08
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07, 24 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records (NSAID course; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-18)
- [Any other records my surgeon's office provides]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
